reconcile.note: Gill reads Leviticus's ban on a brother's wife as excluding the childless-widow case Deuteronomy's levirate law separately commands.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen notes the Holiness Code tightens marriage-of-relatives prohibitions beyond Deuteronomy, a law-code divergence of which this brother's-wife ruling is one instance.

quotes.text: Stricter demands are also made on the laity for personal holiness, especially as regards continence from the sins of the flesh, and the marriage of relatives (Leviticus xviii. xx.). Marriage with an uncle's wife is forbidden (xviii. 14, xx. 20), whereas in Deuteronomy it is still legal.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on the Holiness Code's marriage-of-relatives prohibitions diverging from Deuteronomy.

sides.snippet: If a man takes his brother's wife, it is an impurity: he has uncovered his brother's nakedness; they shall be childless.
sides.verseText: \"'If a man takes his brother's wife, it is an impurity: he has uncovered his brother's nakedness; they shall be childless.

sides.snippet: If brothers dwell together, and one of them die, and have no son… her husband's brother shall go in to her, and take her to him as wife, and perform the duty of a husband's brother to her.
sides.verseText: If brothers dwell together, and one of them die, and have no son, the wife of the dead shall not be married outside to a stranger: her husband's brother shall go in to her, and take her to him as wife, and perform the duty of a husband's brother to her.
